correctness.rationale: For any norm-square-summable Kraus family, norm convergence on B(H), K(H) and S_p follows from the same summability. Finite-rank Kraus truncations prove compactness if coefficients compact; noncompact coefficient forces images of rank-one orthogonal projections to remain norm≥ε² while converging weak-operator to zero, prohibiting compactness on each ideal. Apply to all length-m words, reversing word order for Ψ. Common finite-dimensional Kraus approximants are Hilbert–Schmidt adjoints and each self-conjugate via A↦A*, giving the same nonzero spectrum with multiplicities; norm-stable finite-rank Riesz projections transfer across ideals. Gelfand formula and positivity yield row/column equality, including radius zero. Checked exact characteristic polynomials for three independent noncommuting 2×2 pairs; these do not settle operator-space compactness.
residual_risks: Finite/countable squared-norm-summable Kraus tuples, complex Hilbert H and 1≤p<∞, compact powers only; no general strong-only summability and not all radius-equal tuples.
Finite computations and source package self-checks do not establish infinite quantifiers; reconstructed proof supplies those claims.

originality.rationale: Scherer–Shalit–Shamovich 2026 establish finite-matrix row/column radius equality and infinite-dimensional failure. Fong–Sourour 1979 Theorem 2 already characterizes compact finite elementary operators; Vala earlier gives single AXB. The assessed joint statement is stronger and different: norm-square-summable countable Kraus families; every length-m compact word equivalence to power compactness on each ideal; equality of full nonzero Riesz eigenvalue multisets of compact powers across B(H), K(H), all Banach Schatten classes; resulting row/column radius recovery for some noncompact generator families. This synthesis was not found as a stated theorem in checked primary texts.
residual_risks: Another classical theorem on compact CP duality might already state ideal-independent Riesz spectra or imply this precise synthesis.
Non-summable merely strong Kraus decompositions and arbitrary tuples with matching radii are outside scope.

value.rationale: The exact finite-versus-infinite row/column radius discrepancy is a recognized operator-space obstruction. Fixed-word compactness provides a motivated structural recovery class permitting genuinely noncompact, noncommuting generators with nonzero radius. Equivalence across B(H), K(H), S_p and matching nonzero Riesz multiplicities is stronger than merely numerical radius equality; infinite isometry witnesses show a hypothesis is necessary.
